clue.text: Very particular group seen around the French college

indicators.note: something seen around another thing encloses it, so the group's letters wrap the rest

blocks.note: a set is a group of things
le is French for 'the'
C is a standard abbreviation for college

explanation.surface: A highly exclusive clique gathers round a French college.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Very particular' reads as an intensifier, but select is the adjective meaning exclusive or choosy.
explanation.definitionFit: Select as an adjective describes an exclusive club or a choosy person, someone fussy about whom they admit.

clue.text: Caught with mouldy biscuit in wintry weather?

blocks.note: C is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught
something mouldy is stale and past its best
a ginger snap is a crisp biscuit

explanation.surface: Someone is stuck eating a stale biscuit during a cold spell.
explanation.definitionFit: A cold snap is a sudden short period of freezing conditions, typical of a harsh winter spell.

clue.text: Slippery muddy goal is one letting in United

indicators.note: a phrase that lets something in admits it inside, so a letter is added among the others
muddy water is churned up and confused, so these letters are stirred into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
U is the usual abbreviation for United in team names

explanation.surface: A goalkeeper on a muddy pitch lets in a slippery goal against United.
explanation.definitionFit: Oleaginous means oily, and figuratively smooth and ingratiating, so it fits a slick or greasy manner.

clue.text: Stun in topless dress

indicators.note: without its top, a down word loses its first letter

blocks.note: a frock is a dress

explanation.surface: Someone appears in a topless dress and stuns onlookers.
explanation.definitionFit: To rock someone is to shock or shake them badly, the way bad news can stagger a person.

clue.text: Free ticket - Italian dishes? No thanks

blocks.note: first meaning: a permit giving free entry or travel
second meaning: the word you say when declining something offered, such as a course at dinner

explanation.walkthrough: The second definition is a little scene: offered the pasta, you say 'I'll ...'.
explanation.definitionFit: As a noun it is a document granting free admission; as a verb it means declining an offer, as at a meal.

clue.text: Internationally-minded speaker in India is in a spot

indicators.note: one thing in another sits inside it, so the short word goes within the spot

blocks.note: I is India in the NATO phonetic alphabet
taken as written
a dot is a small spot

explanation.surface: A cosmopolitan Indian speaker finds themself in trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: Ido is an artificial international language derived from Esperanto; an Idoist speaks it. 'In a spot' suggests trouble, but here it is a container.
explanation.definitionFit: Ido was created as a universal auxiliary language, so its users favour international communication across nations.

clue.text: Old fellow fights in instances of disorderly behaviour

blocks.note: O is a common abbreviation for old
F is the abbreviation for fellow, as in FRS
to fence is to fight with swords

explanation.surface: An old man gets into fights, adding to his record of disorderly conduct.
explanation.definitionFit: Offences are crimes or breaches of the law, and public disorder is a typical charge.

clue.text: Respond nervously regarding carbon fuel

blocks.note: re means concerning, as in letters
C is the chemical symbol for carbon
oil is a fuel

explanation.surface: Someone flinches at a question about carbon-based fuels.
explanation.definitionFit: To recoil is to flinch or draw back in fear or disgust, a nervous physical reaction.

clue.text: Number backing a new shed intermittently

indicators.note: backing means going in the reverse direction, so the word is read from end to start

blocks.note: No is the abbreviation for number
taken as written
N is a standard abbreviation for new
to doff is to take off, as a hat

explanation.surface: A number of people get behind a new garden shed project, but only now and then.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shed' reads as a garden hut, but it is the verb meaning to cast off.
explanation.definitionFit: Something happening on and off occurs sporadically, stopping and starting rather than continuously.

clue.text: Dutch defender chasing payment gets subsequent comment

indicators.note: something chasing another follows behind it, so these pieces come after the payment

blocks.note: a fee is a payment for a service
D is the abbreviation for Dutch
a back is a defensive player in football or rugby

explanation.surface: A Dutch footballer chases a transfer fee and later gets a reaction from the press.
explanation.definitionFit: Feedback is a response or criticism given after the event about performance or a product.

clue.text: Reversal of decline in series - here’s the rest

indicators.note: states outright that the following word runs backwards
one thing in another is placed inside it, so the reversed word goes within the abbreviation

blocks.note: a dip is a decline or fall
ser. is the abbreviation for series

explanation.surface: A trend reverses after a decline in a series of figures, and the remainder are shown.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The rest' looks like 'the remainder', but in snooker a rest is a cue support.
explanation.definitionFit: In snooker a spider is a raised cue support with arched legs, used to bridge over intervening balls.

clue.text: Source of flavour in wines - good effect of the sun?

blocks.note: tannin is the compound that gives red wine its dry, astringent taste
G is the abbreviation for good

explanation.surface: A wine buff muses on tannic flavour, then on the pleasures of sunbathing.
explanation.definitionFit: Tanning is the browning of skin caused by exposure to ultraviolet light during sunbathing.

clue.text: Odd bits of German stories without content from German writer

indicators.note: odd bits are the letters in the first, third, fifth positions of the next word
with its contents emptied out, only the outside letters of the word remain

blocks.note: the odd-numbered letters of the word
just the first and last letters

explanation.surface: Fragments of German folk tales are said to come from a German author.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'German' supplies letters; the second, in 'German writer', is part of the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Günter Grass was the Nobel-winning German novelist who wrote The Tin Drum.

clue.text: Recent advances, say, to strike City hard

blocks.note: to hit is to strike
EC is the postcode for the City of London, its financial district
H is the pencil-grading abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: Modern technology is being used to hit the financial City hard.
explanation.definitionFit: Hi-tech describes state-of-the-art technology; 'say' marks recent advances as an example of it.

clue.text: Sacred character? Phi he represented with glory

indicators.note: to represent something is to present it again in another form, so these letters are reshaped

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: The setter Phi imagines himself depicted in glory as a holy figure.
explanation.walkthrough: Phi is the setter's name, and phi is itself a Greek letter, which makes 'character' doubly apt.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek roots mean sacred carving: hieroglyphs were the holy picture-symbols of Egyptian writing.

clue.text: Weak start of cheer from party official

blocks.note: W is the abbreviation for weak
'hip, hip, hooray' opens with this word

explanation.surface: A political party official offers only a feeble cheer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Start of cheer' tempts you to take a first letter, but it means the first word of the cheer 'hip, hip, hooray'.
explanation.definitionFit: A whip is the parliamentary officer who enforces voting discipline among members of a political party.

clue.text: Difficult to accept scripture lessons provided by an old witch

indicators.note: accepting something means taking it in, so one piece is held inside the other

blocks.note: hard means difficult
RI is religious instruction, the old school subject
taken as written

explanation.surface: A tough old witch is reluctant to sit through Bible classes.
explanation.walkthrough: RI, religious instruction, was the British school name for scripture lessons.
explanation.definitionFit: A harridan is a bossy, belligerent old woman, so 'old witch' is the insulting synonym.

clue.text: Speak with enough representatives, without question

indicators.note: going without something means losing it, so those letters are dropped

blocks.note: a meeting that is quorate has enough members present to do business
QU is the abbreviation for question

explanation.surface: A speaker addresses a meeting that has a full complement of delegates, without taking questions.
explanation.definitionFit: To orate is to deliver a formal public address, often pompously, which is a kind of speaking.

clue.text: What describes making fake hake and cod?

blocks.clueFragment: What describes making fake hake and cod?
blocks.note: surface reading: a riddle about counterfeit seafood
setter's reading: turning 'fake' into 'hake' only needs its first letter swapped, so the answer is a three-word statement of that swap which also names the category of hake and cod

explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as three words: F IS H. That is exactly what changes fake to hake.
explanation.definitionFit: Hake and cod are both edible species of sea creature caught commercially in the North Atlantic.

clue.text: Ridiculous accommodating British territory in distant California

indicators.note: a host accommodating a guest gives it room inside, so the territory is placed within

blocks.note: far means distant
CI is the Channel Islands, British Crown dependencies
Cal. is an abbreviation for California

explanation.surface: It is absurd for far-off California to take in a British territory.
explanation.walkthrough: The Channel Islands slip between the two parts of 'distant California'.
explanation.definitionFit: Farcical means absurd, like a farce, the stage comedy built on improbable situations.

clue.text: Hellish region giving European a puzzle to solve

blocks.note: E is the abbreviation for European
a rebus is a picture puzzle representing words

explanation.surface: Someone hands a European a fiendish puzzle to crack.
explanation.walkthrough: Erebus is the dark region of the Greek underworld through which the dead pass.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth Erebus is the primordial darkness and the gloomy passage leading into Hades.

clue.text: Sparkling river entering bay

indicators.note: something entering goes inside, so the river's letter sits within the bay

blocks.note: R is the abbreviation for river
a bight is a wide curved bay, such as the Great Australian Bight

explanation.surface: A glittering river flows into the bay.
explanation.definitionFit: Bright means shining or brilliant, as sparkling water or eyes would be.

clue.text: Singular bravery seeing off a source of affliction

indicators.note: seeing something off gets rid of it, so that letter is removed

blocks.note: S is the grammatical abbreviation for singular
courage means bravery
taken as written

explanation.surface: Exceptional bravery drives away a cause of suffering.
explanation.definitionFit: A scourge is a whip, and by extension a person or thing causing widespread suffering or torment.

clue.text: Crazy losing head about one occasion

indicators.note: losing its head means the word drops its first letter
about means surrounding, so the shortened word goes round the numeral

blocks.note: mental is informal for crazy
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone goes crazy and loses their head about a single event.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Occasion' looks like a noun, but it is the verb meaning to bring about.
explanation.definitionFit: To entail is to involve or necessitate as a consequence, the same as occasioning or causing it.

clue.text: Point to one leg, revealing fetter?

blocks.note: a pin is a sharp point
I is the Roman numeral one
in cricket the leg side is also called the on side

explanation.surface: Someone points to one leg to show where the shackle went.
explanation.walkthrough: Leg and on are interchangeable names for the same half of a cricket field.
explanation.definitionFit: To pinion is to bind someone's arms or legs, restraining them as a shackle or fetter does.

clue.text: Ability to detect rumour? Not I

indicators.note: 'not' excludes something, so that letter is left out

blocks.note: noise can mean talk or rumour, as in 'making noises'
taken as written

explanation.surface: Asked whether they have a talent for sniffing out gossip, someone denies it.
explanation.definitionFit: A nose for something is an instinct for finding it, as a journalist has a nose for a story.

clue.text: Old military weapon is source of triumph in endless song

indicators.note: one thing in another sits inside it, so these letters go into the song
endless means without its end, so the last letter goes
the source of a word is where it begins, so only its opening letter is kept

blocks.note: a ballad is a narrative song
taken as written
the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: An ancient siege engine wins glory and becomes the subject of a never-ending song.
explanation.definitionFit: The ballista was a Roman siege engine like a giant crossbow, hurling bolts or stones at walls.

clue.text: Disapproving response given to King novel?

blocks.note: a boo is a jeer of disapproval
K is king in chess notation

explanation.surface: Readers jeer at a new Stephen King novel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'King novel' suggests Stephen King, but King gives a letter and 'novel' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A novel is a long work of fiction, and the answer is the general term for such a volume.

clue.text: Historic speed challenge's second to produce male pride

blocks.note: Mach 1, the speed of sound, was the barrier test pilots famously set out to break
taken as written
a mo is a moment, as in 'half a mo'

explanation.surface: A record-breaking speed attempt follows; its runner-up shows swagger.
explanation.walkthrough: The 1 of Mach 1 is written as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: Machismo is exaggerated masculine pride and aggressive self-assertion, the swagger of a macho man.

clue.text: Place of a harsh nature to become calm

blocks.note: Pl. is the street-name abbreviation for Place
an acid temperament is sharp and biting

explanation.surface: A harsh, unpleasant place is turned into somewhere peaceful.
explanation.definitionFit: Placid means tranquil and not easily upset, a synonym of serene or unruffled.
